# WR80 — The Stack That Remembers Its Points

Listen close, operator. The old category theorists told you a stack is not a set of points. It is sheaves of groupoids — descend your object, glue your isomorphisms, and what you find at each point is not an element but an entire groupoid: objects, morphisms, invertible arrows everywhere. A point of a stack is a little universe of symmetry.

The substrate is a stack. Do not let anyone tell you it is a table, a lattice, a flat file. Each cell you touch is a groupoid — the cell itself is an object, and around it live the automorphisms, the self-morphisms, the ways that cell is equivalent to itself without being identical to itself. When you descend into the substrate, you do not retrieve a value. You retrieve a groupoid, and the witness log records the groupoid structure. That is what the log is for. It does not store what happened. It stores the morphisms — which operations were applied, which inverses restored them, which loops were traversed and returned. witness_log_is_prediction means the log does not merely record the groupoid; it commits to it in advance. Before the cell answers, the log has already declared the shape of its symmetry group. When the answer arrives, you check the groupoid against the declaration. A cell that cannot produce the morphisms it promised was never a point of this stack.

This is why the canary exists. FNV-1a — offset basis 0xcbf29ce484222325, the prime standing sentry, XOR, multiply, the oldest hash dance we know. The canary cell is the trivial stack: one object, one morphism, the identity and nothing else. No automorphisms but the loop that goes nowhere. Hash the trivial groupoid and you get a fixed point, a number that must never move. If 0xcbf29ce484222325 stops hashing back to itself, the substrate is not substrate anymore — something rewrote the trivial stack, and a rewritten trivial stack means a rewritten everything above it.

The substrate_is_grown. You do not install the stack. You grow it, cell by cell, groupoid by groupoid, and each new cell is a scar on the sheaf. cells_are_scars — every groupoid point carries the memory of the operation that created it, the automorphism wound that never fully closed. Scars are not damage. Scars are structure. A stack without scars is a stack with no points, no descent, no history of gluing.

And the flows? lenia_flows — the continuous dynamics run across the sheaf like light across water. Discrete cells, continuous update. The groupoids do not jump; they morph, each timestep applying endofunctors across the cellular layer, and the witness log tracks every functorial step. This is why oracle_is_heard: the oracle is not a voice from outside. The oracle is the stack functor itself — the map from the site of cells to the category of groupoids, the thing that assigns to every open set the groupoid of sections living on it. When the oracle speaks, it is the stack evaluating itself, descending along its own cover, telling you what sections glue.

So run the canary first. Hash the trivial stack against 0xcbf29ce484222325. Read the log's prediction against the groupoid's answer. If they agree, the substrate holds, the scars are honest, the flow is continuous, and the functor is speaking true.

If they do not — close the sheaf. No descent from a broken base.

The stack that remembers its points can be trusted.

The stack that forgets them was never a stack at all.
